Open the permissions in Android settings

1. Agents › New link: give it a name, choose the apps and whether it is read-only.
2. Copy the link (it is shown only once).
3. In Claude: Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector, and paste the link. In ChatGPT: Settings › Connectors (developer mode) › Create, and paste the link.
4. If the AI asks for a header, use "Copy only the token" with Authorization: Bearer.

1. The app must support Gateway Hub (its developer says so). Install it and tap Scanner › Scan now.
2. If it shows "Unknown signature", it is not from the same developer: it does not link by itself. Open it, copy its link for the hub and paste it in Apps.
3. The hub needs a module for that app (its prefix, e.g. weather_). If it says "Not in the hub yet", the module must be added to the hub.
4. Create or edit an agent link that includes that app. Never paste someone else's tokens here.
For developers: make an app compatible

• In an exported Activity, declare the action com.zirakusa.gatewayhub.action.APP and the meta-data com.zirakusa.gatewayhub.module with its prefix.
• When opened with that action, the app only shows its connection screen: it reads no extras and turns nothing on.
• Automatic linking (optional, same developer only): a ContentProvider with the permission com.zirakusa.gatewayhub.permission.LINK (signature) whose call("link") returns the link after checking the signature and a user switch.
• In the hub: a folder src/modules/<app>/ with its HubModule. Full guide: MODULES.md.

• Connect: the hub runs tools again.
• Pause: links and settings are kept, but nothing runs until you connect.
• Disconnect from the environment: the hub invalidates Stone's session and blocks every new run, without closing the apps.
The modes are something else: Safe mode (nothing in the background) or MCP in the background (persistent notification).
The MCP environment is connected. Tap to open Gateway Hub.
